transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, thank you for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up time someone else needs more. But, um... well, they actually sent me here from occupational health at my job. 

I work in fabrication, running presses all day, and... they said they were worried because my weight is, well, they said it was dangerously low for the kind of physical work I do. I didn't really see it that way, to be honest. I honestly just thought I was finally getting a bit leaner and, you know, more disciplined with myself. 

Is it alright that I came in for that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Have you noticed yourself losing weight recently, and if so, was this weight loss intentional or unintentional?

Um, well, yes, I suppose I have lost some weight. But it wasn't... I mean, I wouldn't call it some big intentional thing where I set out to lose a bunch of weight. I just wanted to be a bit healthier, you know? More mindful. 

I guess I have been pretty careful about what I eat. Most days, I just have coffee before my early shift starts. It wakes me up and gets me going. And then at lunch, I might have, like, half a protein bar just to keep my energy up for the presses. Then after my yoga class in the evenings, I usually just have a small bowl of vegetables. 

I just... if I eat more than that, I start to feel really sluggish and just sort of out of control for the rest of the day. Does that make sense? I just like to keep things manageable. Is that... is that an okay way to explain it?
Do you find yourself afraid of gaining weight or being overweight, even if others might tell you that you're already underweight?

Um... well, I don't know if "afraid" is exactly how I'd put it. I really don't want to sound, you know, irrational or anything. I just... 

I guess, to be completely honest with you... if I step on the scale and it goes up, even just a tiny bit, I do sort of... panic. It's just that I worry so much that I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so incredibly hard for, and... and just end up heavy again. 

People at the shop say what they say about my weight, but they don't know how hard it is to maintain this discipline. I just can't let myself slip and go backward. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just really want to give you a helpful answer.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to control your weight or shape?

Um... no, no I haven't done anything like that. I would never want to do something... you know, extreme or harmful to my body. I just try to stick to my routine and be really disciplined with my meals and my yoga. 

I know some people use those things, but I really just prefer to keep it natural and just... manage it myself through hard work. I hope that's the right answer? I just want you to know I'm not doing anything reckless like that. Is it okay that I just rely on my own discipline?
Do you feel that you have to exercise beyond what is necessary, even when you're tired or not in the mood, to manage your weight or feel in control?

Um, well... I do exercise, yes. I go to my yoga class every evening after my shift at the shop. But I wouldn't call it... I wouldn't say it's beyond what's necessary. It's just part of my routine, you know? 

I mean, sure, sometimes I'm tired after standing at the presses all day, and maybe I don't always feel like going. But I push through because... well, because it's good for me. It helps me unwind and stay focused. It's just about being dedicated, right? 

I don't think I do it just to control my weight, it's just... it's just important to me to stay active and healthy. I wouldn't say it's anything excessive or... or out of the ordinary. A lot of people work out every day, right? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong. I'm just trying to be responsible about my health. Is that... does that sound like a normal amount of exercise to you?
Do you feel that your body shape or weight influences how you see yourself, or affects your self-worth, even if others might not see it the same way?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound vain, or like I'm completely obsessed with my appearance. I know I should be focusing on my work and, you know, more important things. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest with you... yes, it does affect me. 

Sometimes, if I catch a glimpse of myself in the shop window, or even just in the bathroom mirror at work... all I can focus on is my stomach and my thighs. They just... they still look too big to me, even if other people say otherwise. And if I see that, it kind of... well, it can really ruin how I feel about myself for the rest of the entire day. It just makes me feel like I'm failing, somehow, like I'm not working hard enough.

I feel terrible admitting that out loud. It sounds so shallow, doesn't it? I really hope you don't think less of me for saying that. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me. Is it... is it normal to let something like that get to you so much?
